theme.title: One year apart
theme.subtitle: The 2008 and 2009 Finals
theme.recap: The Lakers lost a 21-point first-quarter lead to Boston in 2008, then came back to win the 2009 title.

questions.prompt: The 2009 title was which championship in Lakers history?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Lakers defeated the Magic in five games to win the franchise's 15th NBA championship

questions.prompt: Kobe Bryant won 2009 Finals MVP. What did he average in the series?
questions.context: 2009 NBA Finals · five games vs Orlando

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Bryant averaged 32.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 7.4 assists per game during the series

questions.prompt: The Lakers and Magic set a Finals record low for combined first-quarter points in Game 2 of 2009. What was it?
questions.context: 2009 NBA Finals · Game 2 · at Los Angeles

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: setting a record-low for combined score (30) in the first quarter of an NBA Finals game

questions.prompt: The defending champion Celtics set a franchise-record winning streak in 2008–09. How long was it?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: bringing an end to their franchise-high 19-game winning streak

questions.prompt: In Game 4 of the 2008 Finals, the Lakers set a Finals record for a first-quarter lead. How big was it?
questions.note: 21 points, 35–14. Boston came back to win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: a 35–14 lead after the first quarter, which was the largest first-quarter lead in NBA Finals history
